title: Malaysia Ends Visa-Free Entry for Indians From January 1, 2027; Applications Open December 1
excerpt: Malaysia's Immigration Department will discontinue the 30-day visa exemption for Indian citizens from January 1, 2027. Applications open December 1, 2026 on the MyVISA portal — and it is your arrival date, not your booking date, that decides whether you need one.
body:
• Malaysia will end visa-free entry for Indian passport holders from January 1, 2027; anyone arriving on or after that date must hold a valid Malaysian visa obtained before travel, the Immigration Department of Malaysia (JIM) said in a notice dated November 17, 2026.
  • Visa applications open on December 1, 2026 through the official MyVISA portal — a one-month window before the new rule takes effect.
  • Until December 31, 2026, nothing changes: Indians can still enter visa-free for stays of up to 30 days for tourism, business, social visits and transit.
  • What decides your case is your arrival date, not your departure or booking date: leave India on December 31 but land in Malaysia on January 1, and you need a visa.

Indian passport holders will need a visa to enter Malaysia from January 1, 2027, ending the 30-day visa-free facility that has been in place for tourism and social visits. Malaysia's Immigration Department (JIM) confirmed in a notice dated November 17, 2026 that the visa exemption facility for Indian citizens will be discontinued from January 1, 2027, and that travellers arriving on or after that date must obtain a valid Malaysian visa before departure.

Who is affected — and who is not

The change affects Indian passport holders entering Malaysia on or after January 1, 2027, for the short visits the exemption currently covers: tourism, business, social visits and transit, for stays of up to 30 days. The exemption never permitted employment or study, and that does not change.

It does not affect travel completed under the current rules. Until December 31, 2026, eligible Indian passport holders can continue to enter without a visa for up to 30 days, subject to Malaysia's entry conditions. The test is the date you enter Malaysia: a traveller who departs India on December 31 but arrives in Kuala Lumpur on January 1, 2027 will need a visa, even if the ticket was booked months earlier.

What changes, precisely

Counted here: the entry permission for Indian nationals arriving from January 1, 2027. Not counted: the Malaysia Digital Arrival Card (MDAC), which is a separate requirement and remains in place — travellers must still submit the MDAC online within three days before arrival, even after obtaining a visa.

From January 1, the official MyVISA portal lists India among the nationalities requiring a Single Entry Visa (SEV) for social visits, including tourism, visiting family and friends, and attending short-term events. Applications are handled through Malaysia's official electronic visa platform, the MyVISA portal run by the Immigration Department of Malaysia, which will start accepting applications from Indian nationals on December 1, 2026.

What to do next

If you are travelling to Malaysia in December 2026 and entering by December 31, you can still use the visa exemption, provided you meet the current entry conditions: a passport valid for at least six months, a confirmed return or onward ticket, confirmed accommodation, and the MDAC submitted within three days before arrival.

If any part of your trip has you entering Malaysia on or after January 1, 2027, apply through the MyVISA portal once applications open on December 1. For the eVisa process, applicants should prepare a recent passport-size photograph, the passport biodata page (with at least six months' validity), a confirmed return flight ticket where applicable, proof of paid accommodation, a birth certificate for applicants below 18, and proof of financial support where requested; immigration authorities may ask for further documents in individual cases.

On timing: the standard eVisa processing period under the current MyVISA terms is 2 to 7 working days after complete submission and payment, and Malaysia's immigration authorities instruct applicants to apply at least 14 days before their intended travel date. Two cautions from the official terms: all visa payments are strictly non-refundable, whether an application is approved or rejected, and the November 17 announcement does not specify the visa fee that will apply to Indian nationals — check the fee shown on the portal when applications open on December 1. Travellers should also carry the approved eVisa, passport, return ticket and accommodation confirmation when they travel, and submit the Malaysia Digital Arrival Card within three days before arrival.

Why Malaysia is a big route for Indian travellers

Malaysia received 1.56 million Indian tourist arrivals in 2025, and recorded 738,000 arrivals from India between January and June this year, placing India among its top five tourism source markets alongside China, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia, according to Tourism Malaysia figures reported by India Outbound. Tourism Malaysia had set a target — a target, not an outcome — of 2.1 million Indian tourists in 2026, with more than 190 direct flights a week connecting India and Malaysia.

The end of the exemption also follows a warning from India's own mission. In September 2026, the High Commission of India in Kuala Lumpur cautioned Indian nationals against using the 30-day visa-free facility to seek employment in Malaysia, warned of unscrupulous agents making false employment promises, and clarified that the facility was for tourism and social visits and did not permit travellers to take up work; those seeking jobs must obtain the appropriate work authorisation before travelling.
